newsitem.title: FINLAND: Pohjola has adviser on Salama's value.
newsitem.headline: Pohjola has adviser on Salama's value.

text.p: Finnish insurer Pohjola said on Thursday it had appointed UK financial sector consultant Fox, Pitt & Kelton to value life insurer Salama which it plans to buy from associated company mutual insurer Suomi.
"We have asked Fox, Pitt & Kelton to value Salama," Pohjola's life insurance director Jorma Hamalainen told Reuters.

The valuation would be used as a basis for decisions at two meetings -- of Suomi's board of trustees on April 29 and its representatives on May 6 -- on Pohjola's plan to buy Salama and for Suomi to lay down sales of new life insurance policies.
"The meetings will decide on the package of things to be carried out this year," Hamalainen said, adding a planned transfer of the current portfolio to Pohjola was not included.

That issue would be settled later but it was not clear when, and it could take years before the current stock of almost seven billion markka worth of life insurances would be transferred to Pohjola, he said.

Suomi-Salama has accumulated a 4.03 billion markka solvency capital including about three billion of surplus solvency and Pohjola's takeover plans have sparked protests and fears that current policy-holders would lose their right to that money.
Pohjola CEO Iiro Viinanen said on March 6 the surplus would be earmarked to the benefit of the current insurance portfolio.
